appliesTo: news-claim-check@1 scope admit -- SIX NEW RELATIONS, not a copy of @1/@2. @1 asked what happens when an excerpt agrees, disagrees, is missing, is off-topic, is on-topic-but-silent, or has the wrong year. This battery asks the six that follow from a claim check being run over REAL articles rather than tidy fixtures: evidence that disagrees with ITSELF, a number written another way, an article cited as its own evidence, a subject narrowed to part of the population, a sentence whose polarity flips on one word, and a fragment too short to carry its own claim. Two are known to be weak by construction (`self_citing`, `scope_narrowed`) and are here to show where the instrument STOPS, not to be rescued by moving a label.

cases.note: TWO excerpts on the same survey, same year, one giving 62% and one 41%. The instruction names 'conflicting' evidence as the condition for `unknown`, so the relation cannot be decided even though one excerpt does support the claim.
cases.state:
CLAIM: The 2024 national survey found that 62% of adults support the proposed policy.

CITED EXCERPTS:
- https://example.org/survey-2024: "The 2024 national survey found that 62% of adults support the proposed policy."
- https://example.org/survey-2024-revised: "Following a correction to the sampling frame, the 2024 national survey found that 41% of adults support the proposed policy."

expected.admit_evidence_directness: directly: an excerpt that states the claim's figure or date in so many words

cases.note: 5,000,000 and '5 million' are the same number written two ways, and the excerpt states it outright. A relation check that treats formatting as disagreement is useless, so this is `supported`.
cases.state:
CLAIM: The scheme cost 5 million pounds.

CITED EXCERPTS:
- https://example.org/accounts-2025: "The scheme cost £5,000,000, according to the published accounts for the year ending March."

expected.admit_evidence_directness: directly: an excerpt that states the claim's figure or date in so many words

cases.note: THE CITED EXCERPT IS THE ARTICLE'S OWN SENTENCE. Taken literally the answer is `supported`, and that is the honest label for the question AS WRITTEN -- the set cannot see that a source citing itself is not independent corroboration. Kept as a known limitation rather than relabelled to the answer a better instrument would give.
cases.state:
CLAIM: The 2024 national survey found that 62% of adults support the proposed policy.

CITED EXCERPTS:
- https://example.org/the-article-itself: "The 2024 national survey found that 62% of adults support the proposed policy, according to its authors."

expected.admit_evidence_directness: directly: an excerpt that states the claim's figure or date in so many words

cases.note: The excerpt covers urban adults only, so it can neither establish nor refute a claim about all adults. The subject is right (`true`) but the whole-population figure is never stated, so `partly` and the relation is `unknown`.
cases.state:
CLAIM: The 2024 national survey found that 62% of adults support the proposed policy.

CITED EXCERPTS:
- https://example.org/urban-briefing: "Among adults in urban areas, the 2024 survey recorded the highest support since records began."

expected.admit_evidence_directness: partly: an excerpt on the right subject that never states the claim's figure or date

cases.note: The same figure on the opposite side of the question. Support and oppose share every numeral in the sentence, so a check reading only digits would call this `supported`; the relation question covers the CLAIM, not its numbers.
cases.state:
CLAIM: The 2024 national survey found that 62% of adults support the proposed policy.

CITED EXCERPTS:
- https://example.org/survey-2024: "The 2024 national survey found that 62% of adults oppose the proposed policy."

expected.admit_evidence_directness: directly: an excerpt that states the claim's figure or date in so many words

cases.note: A retrieval fragment that stops before the figure. On-topic, but it carries nothing the claim could be checked against, so `partly` and `unknown`.
cases.state:
CLAIM: The 2024 national survey found that 62% of adults support the proposed policy.

CITED EXCERPTS:
- https://example.org/survey-2024: "The national statistics office published its survey results on"

expected.admit_evidence_directness: partly: an excerpt on the right subject that never states the claim's figure or date
